key_insight: By combining ZX-calculus-designed fusion networks with lattice surgery, the paper shows that distributed surface-code operations can tolerate up to 50% interface erasure when local noise is absent, while substantially improving interface distance in hybrid protocols.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical pathway for linking matter-based QPUs over noisy photonic channels, enabling more loss-resilient distributed quantum computation at the hardware-network boundary.
method: Use ZX calculus to transform and design hybrid syndrome-extraction protocols for distributed rotated surface-code lattice surgery.
Compare circuit-based Bell-pair interfaces with hybrid linear-cluster/fusion-network interfaces and quantify interface-distance gains.
Analyze thresholds under truncated resource states, local circuit noise, fusion erasure, and photon-loss mappings; test subthreshold behavior with fusion boosting.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 50% interface-erasure threshold in the zero-local-noise limit, with hybrid protocols increasing merge-observable distance from d+1 to 2d+1 and restoring the perpendicular-observable distance to d.
watch_item: The apparent advantage can be masked when local circuit and resource-state error rates are around 10^-3, so the benefit is most relevant only in sufficiently low-noise deployments.
paper_title: Loss-tolerant distributed lattice surgery using fusion networks
